problemStatement.formal: For continuous f: Sⁿ → ℝⁿ and ε > 0, finding x ∈ Sⁿ with ‖f(x) - f(-x)‖ < ε is PPAD-complete. We formalize the problem, prove exact→approximate reduction, state Tucker's lemma, and define PPAD.
problemStatement.plain: The computational complexity of finding an approximately antipodal pair for a continuous function on the sphere is PPAD-complete. This means it is computationally hard (no polynomial-time algorithm unless PPAD ⊆ P) but a solution is guaranteed to exist.
whyMatters: Tucker's lemma is the combinatorial bridge between topology and computation
Same complexity class as Nash equilibrium computation

proven: Exact antipodal pair implies approximate for any ε > 0
Exact pair gives zero norm difference
Gadget function (f(x) - f(-x)) Lipschitz bound: 2L for L-Lipschitz f
axiomatized: Borsuk-Ulam exact theorem (proved in BorsukUlam.lean modulo covering space axiom)
PPAD solution existence (parity argument / handshaking lemma)

insights: The PPAD-completeness of approximate Borsuk-Ulam is via Tucker's lemma: triangulate the sphere with mesh < ε, label vertices by the dominant coordinate of f(x)-f(-x), complementary edges yield approximate antipodal pairs
For fixed dimension n, the running time is polynomial in L/ε (where L is the Lipschitz constant)
For variable dimension, the problem is PPAD-complete - same hardness as Nash equilibrium
The gadget function g(x) = f(x) - f(-x) is odd and 2L-Lipschitz, which bounds the mesh size needed
PPAD captures problems guaranteed by directed parity arguments: a directed graph with a known source must have a sink
